newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada will eye turnout on barley monopoly vote.
newsitem.headline: Canada will eye turnout on barley monopoly vote.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said on Thursday he would examine the level of voter turnout in February's plebiscite on barley marketing to determine whether it was decisive enough to accept.

"We all have to look at the results and determine whether the level of participation is credible," he said, referring to a vote on ending the Canadian Wheat Board monopoly on barley exports and domestic barley sales for human consumption.
He did say that if there were no great aberration and the turnout was good, he would act on a simple majority of votes cast -- i.e., 50 percent plus one vote.
Goodale added that he did not think turnout would be an issue, recalling turnout of more than 80 percent on a vote on whether to include rapeseed in the mandate of the Canadian Wheat Board (CWB).
Reform Party Member of Parliament Leon Benoit said it was undemocratic not to decide in advance what level of turnout was required.

Goodale also said the interim CWB board of directors that the government intends to appoint as part of a revamped CWB structure would be identified early next year. The interim board would take office on August 1.
They would stay on until a farmer-elected majority would take office on August 1, 1998.
